value.loc: Sec. 2 The model, p. 2; Sec. 4.3, p. 10
value.quote: most of the other related papers, we neglect strategic considerations of voters
value.note: The paper states that votes equal preferences (Sec. 2: top preference 'always identical with their votes'; Sec. 4.3: voters 'vote according to their original preference rankings') and justifies this by convention in prior work (Dasgupta and Maskin), which C3.3 codes as CONV, a reason; the remarks that voters may reconsider (Sec. 4.3) or that honest voting may not be compelling (Sec. 4.4) acknowledge a possibility that is then assumed away, not a model treating input and preference as separate objects.

C2.4.reason: The identity of votes and preferences is stated in words and supported by a citation of convention (both coders code C3.3 = CONV), so IDJ fits better than DIST (no separate objects in the model) or IDS (a reason is given).

value.quote: the consideration of preference intensities inferred from ordinal data.
value.note: Applicability met: inputs are rankings (RANK) and the paper uses voters' 'preference intensities' (Borda/MIIA discussion); the relation to ordinal input is mentioned (intensities inferred from ordinal data) but not defined.

C4.1.reason: The paper refers to voters' preference intensities, which triggers C4.1, and only mentions without defining that they are inferred from ordinal rankings.
